problem: Existing VLN methods mostly fuse global visual features with the semantic space. They ignore local highlight regions and the alignment of semantic knowledge, and they mismatch paths when instructions are coarse-grained.
motivation: Local regional cues and keyword-to-visual grounding matter for choosing actions, especially when instructions are coarse. Knowledge-augmented reasoning over image regions plus soft action prompts should improve alignment between instruction and visual space.
key_idea: KRSP maps fine-grained regional image features and text knowledge into a shared sub-space for knowledge-augmented reasoning, uses CoCoOp-derived soft action prompts to align instruction keywords with sub-visual information, and adds a cross-modal feature alignment loss.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that regional knowledge reasoning, soft-prompt alignment and an alignment penalty each help close the gap between instruction and visual features.
method: Regional knowledge reasoning: fine-grained processing of local image regions, mapping context image features and text knowledge into a common sub-space to boost reasoning.
Soft-prompt learning: aligns instruction keywords with sub-visual information to handle path mismatch under coarse-grained instructions.
CoCoOp prompts: a large-scale pre-trained model (CoCoOp) collects highly matched soft action prompts into a unified instruction set.
Cross-modal feature alignment loss: a general loss whose penalty mechanism draws sub-visual information and instruction space closer semantically.
